title: Capacity Harbor: Harmonized Scaling Fabric & Isolation Contracts (PRD draft)
content:
Summary:

This doc proposes a pattern and implementation sketch for a Dedicated capacity autoscaler and tenant isolation mechanism we’re calling "Capacity Harbor" (codename: CEDAR). The goal is to provide predictable latency/throughput guarantees for committed Dedicated customers while allowing safe, observable burst behavior and graceful degradation when capacity is constrained.

Principles / design goals:
- Predictable SLOs for reserved pools: committed tenants keep latency/throughput guarantees within configured windows.
- Elastic but bounded bursts: tenants can exceed committed capacity for short periods without destabilizing the pool.
- Soft isolation contracts: a formalizable per-tenant contract that defines priority, burst budget, decay rules and fallback behavior.
- Operational simplicity: intuitive console controls and clear runbooks for SREs and customer success.
- Measurable economics: per-tenant accounting for consumed burst units and credit-rollback behavior.

Key concepts and components:
1) Harbor Reservoir (reservation layer)
- Each Dedicated pool exposes a Harbor Reservoir: the committed capacity ledger (cores / gpus / concurrency units) + per-tenant credit buckets.
- Reservation is expressed as a set of lanes: steady-lane (reserved), transient-lane (burst), prewarm-lane (preallocated for fast warmstart).
- Reservoir enforces admission control — steady-lane requests are fast-path; transient-lane demand is admitted up to available burst credits and subject to shaping.

2) Harmonized Scaling Fabric (autoscaler behavior)
- Autoscaler operates across two axes: long-horizon resizing (provision more nodes when sustained utilization > threshold for X minutes) and microburst coordination (short-term prewarming and transient overlay).
- Scaling fabric uses signal fusion: demand spikes + queue latencies + KV cache hit rates -> produce a composite urgency score. Thresholds map to actions: prewarm, expand ephemeral, or throttle.
- Important: fabric favors graceful micro-actions first (prewarm ephemeral slots, evict low-priority opportunistic jobs) and only performs heavy node-level scaling when sustained.

3) Isolation Contracts (CEDAR contracts)
- Each tenant has a CEDAR contract: {priority_tier, steady_allocation, burst_budget, decay_window, fallback_policy}. Contracts are pegged to billing and can be negotiated in sales.
- Burst_budget is expressed in burst-units (BUs). BUs track ephemeral tokens consumed on bursts; they decay over a configured window (e.g., linear decay over 24 hours) unless purchased/renewed.
- Fallback_policy enumerates tolerated degradation: 1) best-effort on shared standby model, 2) degrade to a quantized lower-fidelity model, 3) queue with informative SLA messages.

4) Burst Handshake & Throttle Protocol
- When a request would exceed steady_allocation, the Harbor reservoir performs a handshake: check BU, if available, admit with BU decrement and stamp request metadata (traceable). If no BU, consult fallback_policy.
- Throttle handshake supports partial admits: allow reduced concurrency or synthetic latency padding to keep fairness.

5) Observability & Billing
- Telemetry: BU consumption, admission_rate_by_lane, per-tenant tail latency percentiles, prewarm_hit_rate, autoscaler-actions timeline.
- Billing: BU usage becomes a line-item on invoices. Console shows BU balances, projected decay, and one-click BU top-ups.

API & Console surface (proposal)
- API: /reservations.create, /reservations.update (change steady_allocation), /reservations.topup_burst, /reservations.query_balance, /reservations.request_burst (optional explicit).
- Console: single-pane BU ledger, per-tenant contract editor, historical burst timeline, suggested auto-topup thresholds, and what-if simulator (projected BU runout under load).

Operator runbook snippets (SRE + CS)
- If pool steady-lane saturation > 85% for > 10m: autoscaler should trigger warm-slot allocation; alert to oncall and CS for high-burst tenants.
- BU spike without autoscale: check for noisy neighbor signature (sudden many small requests from a single tenant), enforce temporary quarantine or rate-limit.
- Node decomm: drain transient-lane first; move prewarm-lane workloads to new nodes.

Metrics & success criteria (initial)
- 99th percentile latency within committed SLO 99% of the time for steady-lane traffic.
- No more than 2 unplanned pool-wide failovers per quarter attributable to burst overload.
- BU billing accuracy within 1% over monthly rollups.

Rollout plan (phased)
- Phase 0 (research / sim): build simulator that models BUs, decay curves, and burst behavior using historical traffic traces. (2-4 weeks)
- Phase 1 (canary): implement Harbor Reservoir control plane and passive BU accounting on a canary Dedicated pool (no enforcement). Surface console metrics. (4-6 weeks)
- Phase 2 (enforce): enable burst admission and simple fallback policy (best-effort -> queue) for low-risk tenants. Expose BU topups. (4 weeks)
- Phase 3 (GA): full CEDAR contract UI + billing + multi-region support + operator dashboards. (6-8 weeks)

Open questions & tradeoffs:
- Decay model for burst units: linear vs exponential — linear is easier to reason about; exponential penalizes rapid burst cycles more. Need econ input.
- How aggressive should prewarming be? Prewarm too much and we waste capacity; too little and latency suffers. Use ML-driven prewarm heuristics from Optimize team.
- Integration with Dedicated tenancy: should Harbor be an overlay that works across pools (cross-pool BU borrowing) or strictly per-pool? Cross-pool borrowing simplifies utilization but adds complexity and potential for cross-tenant coupling.

Next steps / action items:
- Product: define the CEDAR contract schema and billing mapping (owner: Asha, due: 2025-01-24)
- Infra: build passive BU accounting pipeline and add BU metrics to console (owner: Liam, due: 2025-02-07)
- SRE/Eng: prototype microburst handshake in the request admission path on the canary pool (owner: Noah, due: 2025-02-14)
- Finance: recommend pricing bands for BUs and decay policies (owner: Priya K., due: 2025-02-10)

Notes / links:
- Slack thread: #dedicated-burst-experiments (see pinned messages for sample traces)
- Simulator draft: GH-PR-3214 (internal)
- Related: Prewarm heuristics doc (product/optimize) and existing autoscaler heuristics in serving-runtime repo.

Rough appendix (for follow-up):
- Example CEDAR contract snip: priority=gold, steady=200 concurrency, burst_budget=10k BUs, decay=24h, fallback=degrade-model -> queue
- Example BU accounting: a 2-second request at p95 uses 1 BU; a 20-token generation might use 0.1 BU (we need to normalize BU unit to something like CPU-GPU microseconds equivalent).

This is intentionally a sketch. Want feedback on the contract primitives, BU semantics, and acceptable operator complexity.
